records.quote: Theorem: Suppose X1 ~ TL − TIIEHL − MO − G(b1, α, δ, ξ) and X2 ~ TL − TIIEHL − MO − G(b2, α, δ, ξ). If b1 < b2, then f(x;b1,α,δ,ξ)/f(x;b2,α,δ,ξ) is decreasing in x. ... If b1 < b2, then ∂/∂x [f(x;b1,α,δ,ξ)/f(x;b2,α,δ,ξ)] < 0, which implies that likelihood ratio order exist among X1 and X2, that is, X2 <lr X1.
records.family: Topp-Leone type II exponentiated half logistic–Marshall-Olkin-G family TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b, α, δ, ξ) over baseline G(·;ξ)
records.compared: Topp-Leone parameters b1 < b2; common α, δ, ξ

hypotheses.text: X1 ~ TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b1, α, δ, ξ), X2 ~ TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b2, α, δ, ξ); b1 < b2

conclusion.direction: X2 <=_lr X1 as printed (the ratio f1/f2 decreasing would instead mean X1 <=_lr X2 — see ambiguity)

records.ambiguity: The printed conclusion 'X2 <lr X1' is inconsistent with f1/f2 decreasing, which under the stated definition (f_X/f_Y decreasing ⟹ X <lr Y) gives X1 <lr X2; direction likely transposed in print.

records.quote: As a result, we conclude that X1 and X2 are stochastically ordered, that is, X1 <st X2.
records.compared: b1 < b2; common α, δ, ξ

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_st X2 (as printed; opposite to the printed lr direction)

records.ambiguity: Printed 'X1 <st X2' contradicts the printed 'X2 <lr X1' (since lr ⟹ st same direction); at least one direction is misprinted.

records.quote: Theorem: Suppose X1 ~ TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b1, α, δ, ξ) and X2 ~ TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b2, α, δ, ξ). If b1 < b2, then f(x;b1,α,δ,ξ)/f(x;b2,α,δ,ξ) is decreasing in x. ... If b1 < b2, then ∂/∂x [f(x;b1,α,δ,ξ)/f(x;b2,α,δ,ξ)] < 0, which implies that likelihood ratio order exist among X1 and X2, that is, X2 <lr X1. As a result, we conclude that X1 and X2 are stochastically ordered, that is, X1 <st X2.
records.family: Topp-Leone type II Exponentiated-Half Logistic-Marshall-Olkin-G family TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b,α,δ,ξ)
records.compared: X1 vs X2 differing only in parameter b (b1 < b2; common α, δ, ξ)

conclusion.direction: f(x;b1)/f(x;b2) decreasing in x ⇒ X1 ≤lr X2; paper prints 'X2 <lr X1' and then 'X1 <st X2' — with hr and st consequences per X <lr Y ⟹ X <hr Y ⟹ X <st Y

records.ambiguity: Printed conclusion is internally inconsistent: the decreasing density ratio implies X1 <lr X2 (X1 stochastically smaller), matching the printed 'X1 <st X2', but the paper prints 'X2 <lr X1'. The lr direction appears to be a typo; consistent reading: X1 <lr X2 and X1 <st X2 when b1 < b2.
